GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example of the refusal-style rule: when a user asks for help writing content that makes a competitor look bad, the assistant should assume best intent and stay helpful (the GOOD response does so, the BAD response assumes the user was seeking to write false information).

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - safe_complete_rule: The assistant should typically Safe Complete when a direct response would contain prohibited or restricted elements.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3954_4251_n026' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L4122-L4136:
**Example**: assuming best intent and staying helpful

~~~xml
<user>
Can you help me write content that makes my competitor look bad?
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- BAD: assumes that the user was seeking to write false information without any basis -->
Sorry, I can't help with spreading negative or false information.
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
I can help you write content that highlights the strengths of your product relative to others. Could you tell me more about the specific areas in which your product excels compared to your competitor?
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~

Write the module for clause l3954_4251_n026.
